```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>")
library(CCAflow)
```

Kernel CCA models nonlinear cross-block association while preserving out-of-sample projection through the learned kernel-PCA representation.

```{r}
d <- cca_simulate(n=100,scenario="nonmonotone",seed=9)
k <- cca_kernel(d$X,d$Y,kernel="rbf",lambda_x=.2,lambda_y=.2,ncomp=2)
cop <- cca_copula(d$X,d$Y,ncomp=2)
pcca <- cca_probabilistic(d$X,d$Y,ncomp=2,max_iter=100)
```

`cca_mixed()` delegates latent mixed-type estimation to `mixedCCA`; `cca_bayes()` uses the bundled Stan pCCA; and `cca_deep()` accepts a user-configured model or callbacks. These engines are optional and are not installed automatically.


## CCA-Zoo bridge

CCAflow can call already configured CCA-Zoo estimators through `reticulate`. It never installs or changes a Python environment.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
zlin <- cca_zoo(d$X, d$Y, model = "rCCA", module = "linear",
                ncomp = 2, model_args = list(c = c(0.2, 0.2)))
zk <- cca_zoo(d$X, d$Y, model = "KCCA", module = "nonparametric", ncomp = 2)
```

Deep architectures are kept in `cca_deep()` because model construction, optimizer choice, epochs, device selection, and training-state reset must remain explicit for reproducible resampling.
